messages:
Carmen (Sales): Hey team — Nimbus Partners surfaced a co-sell POC request. Customer wants a joint pilot: Redwood Private deployed into their AWS account (VPC peering), SAML SSO, fixed egress IPs for allowlisting, audit logs retention for 90d, and a 6‑week trial. Partner asks for estimated pilot pricing and a short list of technical blockers. Can eng/infra/security weigh in?

Alex P (Eng): +1. Need clarity on scale: expected rps, max sequence lengths, concurrent users. That will drive Dedicated sizing (GPU counts) and whether we need KV cache sizing.

Carmen (Sales): They said initial load ~20 rps, bursts to 80 for 30m/day, mostly short-chat (<=512 tokens). Pilot customer: 5 internal users, partner will demo to 2 customers.

Samir (Platform): Feasible. For 20–80 rps short sequences, a small dedicated pool (2 x A10-like GPUs) with autoscale burst should be fine for pilot. We need partner AWS account details for VPC peering/subnets + a CIDR to reserve. Also: will they insist on Private control plane or are they okay with customer-managed VPC + our control plane?

Leah T (Partnerships): Nimbus prefers we keep control plane hosted but allow VPC peering to restrict egress. They want to avoid installing on-prem.

Nora (Security): Security asks: 1) SAML metadata for SP/SP-initiated flow; 2) KMS integration for customer key (bring-your-own-key) or confirm we manage keys; 3) SOC2/audit evidence for 90d logs retention. Also need to run their short security questionnaire — I'll take that.

Carmen (Sales): Partner also asked about pricing split — they want a pilot discount and clear handoff to co-sell license afterwards. Any guidance?

Alex P (Eng): For SAML, we need ACS URL + Entity ID from their IdP. We can provide a sample SP metadata. Example SP fields: 

```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://auth.redwood.example/sp">
  <SPSSODescriptor>
    <AssertionConsumerService Location="https://control.redwood.example/saml/acs" Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST"/>
  </SPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```

Also they asked for egress IPs: we can provide a small set of NAT egress IPs for allowlisting. Need to confirm whether they require static IPs per region.

Samir (Platform): For pilot, we can give a fixed egress block of 5 IPs in the region. Example network checklist for them to fill: 
- VPC peering CIDR: e.g., 10.50.0.0/16
- Subnets for control-plane endpoints (public) + private subnets for dataplane
- Security group: allow outbound to our egress IPs on 443
- Route tables: ensure peering routes to Redwood subnets

Carmen (Sales): Leah — can you kick off an ask to Nimbus to fill a short network form with those? I'll attach pricing question doc.

Leah T (Partnerships): On it. I'll send Nimbus the network form + SAML sample and ask for their IdP metadata by EOD. Also coordinating a technical call Thu 10am PT.

Nora (Security): I'll start the security questionnaire in parallel. If they request BYOK, we need KMS key ARN and key policy allowing cross-account use, or they can give us an external key. Either way, flagging this: BYOK adds ~3–5 days to pilot timeline.

Carmen (Sales): Noted. For pricing: propose pilot pricing = flat monthly pilot fee $6k + usage up to a cap (tokens) then overage. Post-pilot: typical co-sell split — partner gets referral credit and we roll into a committed Dedicated contract. Is that workable?

Samir (Platform): That structure is fine. For engineering handoff we should create two artifacts: 1) Pilot runbook (provisioning steps, SAML metadata, egress IPs, telemetry endpoints), 2) Acceptance criteria (latency targets, successful SSO login, audit log visibility). I'll draft the runbook template.

Alex P (Eng): Quick provisioning snippet we can reuse during runbook: 

```bash
# create pilot tenant record
rwctl tenants create --name "nimbus-pilot" --region us-west-2 --plan dedicated-pilot \\\n  --peering-cidr 10.50.0.0/16 --egress-ips 54.23.12.34,54.23.12.35 \\\n  --saml-sp-metadata-file nimbus-sp.xml
```

Leah T (Partnerships): Good. I'll also add an enablement checklist for Nimbus: dashboard walk-through, telemetry cursors, how to invite partner users, run demo scripts.

Carmen (Sales): Who owns pilot billing + contract? I can own the sales side, but need an SOW sketch from legal.

Nora (Security): Tagging legal/sec for SOW review. I can share the questionnaire answers and SOC artifacts.

InfraBot: Provision request created: PR-4872 — initial pilot tenant template queued. Assigned to @Samir. ETA: 2 business days.

Samir (Platform): I'll take PR-4872. Next actions: (1) draft pilot runbook (2) send egress IPs list (3) estimate GPU sizing cost for pilot and a rough monthly committed quote. Expect updates in 48h.

Carmen (Sales): Thanks all. Leah — push the Thu 10am invite and include Samir, Alex, Nora. I'll draft the pricing note for Nimbus and attach it. :pray:

Leah T (Partnerships): Invite sent. Link to meeting: https://meet.example/teams/123-pt.

Carmen (Sales): Closing loop — partner wants the security questionnaire back before Thu if possible. Nora — can you prioritize that?

Nora (Security): Will prioritize, aim to return answers tomorrow EOD.

Alex P (Eng): One more note — telemetry: we need to ensure request-level tracing includes partner id and tenant id. I'll add a small schema change to the runbook for that header: `X-Redwood-Partner: nimbus` and `X-Redwood-Tenant: nimbus-pilot`.

Carmen (Sales): Perfect. I'll follow up with Nimbus and post any updates here.

Samir (Platform): Logged tasks in internal board: https://jira.internal/browse/RWF-1122 (pilot provisioning)

Carmen (Sales): Thanks team — talk soon.
